nonBlockingRisks.body: The new gate-aware `pod-ready` stage is correct, but `pod-running` (here) still writes `Ready=True` unconditionally on the Pending→Running transition, with no gate check. So a pod the controller has gated out (any readiness gate False) can still be briefly exposed as Ready by `pod-running`, then later flipped back to False by `pod-ready-blocked`. That is exactly the flap class this PR removes in production, so the stress sim currently does not faithfully guard against its own regression. Cheapest fix: have `pod-running` write `Ready=False` (set ContainersReady/Initialized/phase=Running only) and let only the gate-aware `pod-ready` stage promote to `Ready=True` — so every Ready=True promotion goes through the gate check. Worth folding into this PR since the KWOK companion is part of the change.

The new `pod-ready-blocked` stage is not in the teardown — lines here delete `pod-initialize`, `pod-running`, `pod-ready`, `pod-delete` but omit `pod-ready-blocked`, so the stage leaks after uninstall. Add `kubectl delete stage pod-ready-blocked --ignore-not-found=true` next to the others.

Confirmed the fix is correct. The premise (issue #460) reproduces at the code/unit layer: base writes the kubelet-owned `Ready` via `util.UpdatePodReadyCondition` here and in `removeNotReadyKey`, making the controller a second writer whose value kubelet's status-manager cache then republishes stale on its 10s sync. Removing both calls (this + line ~99) so the controller writes only the gate is the right fix — it restores the single-writer invariant. Harness-bites check: the new contract tests fail against buggy base (controller rewrites Ready) and pass on this PR head. (I could not trigger the live 25-35ms flap on the ACK cluster — its installed v0.8.0 controller is stuck on unrelated legacy `restartPolicy` data, not because the flap is absent.)

Nice improvement on the test harness. The old `fakeAdapter` recomputed `Ready` the way kubelet would after every write, so it passed both with and without the bug it was meant to guard — the tests never actually pinned the controller's own Ready write. `recordingAdapter` recording writes verbatim, plus the `kubeletManagedReady` marker condition with a distinctive Reason/Message, makes any controller write to Ready show up in `reflect.DeepEqual` even when the Status happens to match. This is the kind of test that would have caught the regression originally.

publishableSummary.body: Production fix is correct and should merge; the KWOK companion needs two small fixes first. Premise confirmed: base writes the kubelet-owned `Ready` from `addNotReadyKey`/`removeNotReadyKey` (a second writer), so kubelet republishes the stale value on its 10s sync — the True→False→True flap. Removing the two `UpdatePodReadyCondition` calls so the controller writes only the readiness gate restores the single-writer invariant; the rewritten tests now actually bite (the old fakeAdapter masked the bug — verified: tests fail on buggy base, pass on this head). On the two remaining `UpdatePodReadyCondition` callers in the in-place paths: the justification is sound in the happy path (each is followed in the same function by a spec/label write that forces kubelet to re-sync), but those are separate, non-atomic API calls, not a transaction — so `Ready=False` can land while the spec/label write fails. I would not delete those callers in this PR, but the failure path is worth a separate follow-up. Two KWOK items to fold in before merge: (1) `pod-running` still writes `Ready=True` unconditionally and bypasses the new gate-aware check, so a gated-out pod can be briefly exposed Ready — have `pod-running` leave `Ready=False` and let only the gate-aware `pod-ready` promote; (2) `pod-ready-blocked` is missing from `teardown-kwok.sh` and leaks after uninstall. Neither touches production code. Verified on branch verify/pr461-pod-ready-kubelet — evidence under docs/verification/pr461-pod-ready-kubelet/.
